author: reek
body: Collation has to be checked against the order it is supposed to produce and against the order it is supposed to REPLACE, or a key that did nothing would look the same as one that worked.

author: reek
body: The accent table names a base letter for each accented form. Its claim is checkable the same way: the accented form's Unicode value is not the base letter's, but the base index it points at must be the index of the letter the accent sits on, which the prose names. Only the count is asserted here; the fold itself is asserted by the ordering lines below.

target: section:Letters, both orders side by side
author: reek
body: Read as collation|encoding. Four of these six disagree.

author: reek
body: An accented letter folds onto its base for the primary weight, so it sorts between that base and the next letter rather than after every letter in the alphabet. The second run then puts the bare letter first.

target: section:A sort, which is the point of a key
author: reek
body: Keys extracted once, compared with the primitive that already existed. Seeded so that neither the seeded order nor encoding order is the answer.
